tutorial_example_entry.lesson_core_move: Compute the convolution of unequal-width rectangular pulses by identifying the edge-aligned breakpoints, expressing the sliding overlap length piecewise, and scaling by the pulse amplitudes to obtain the trapezoidal output.

sections.section_title: Introduction to Convolution of Unequal-Width Rectangular Pulses

image_slots.image_description: Clean instructional signal-plot concept diagram on a horizontal $\tau$-axis. Show a wider fixed rectangular pulse $x(\tau)$ and a shorter rectangular pulse $h(t - \tau)$ sliding across it. Mark the first contact position, the interval where the shorter pulse is fully inside the wider pulse, and the last contact position. Shade one overlap segment and label it $L(t)$. Include simple labels for $\tau$ and t, and avoid decorative styling.

blocks.text: For rectangular pulses, the convolution value at a time t comes from the overlap of two supports on the $\tau$-axis: the fixed support of $x(\tau)$ and the shifted support of $h(t - \tau)$. Since each pulse is constant on its support, the integral is controlled by how long those two supports overlap.

When the two rectangular pulses have unequal widths, the shorter pulse can become completely covered by the longer one. That creates three nonzero overlap behaviors as t increases: the overlap length grows, then stays equal to the shorter width, then shrinks back to zero.

The edge-aligned breakpoints are the t-values where one edge of the sliding support lines up with one edge of the fixed support. These breakpoints split the time axis into no overlap, growing overlap, full overlap, shrinking overlap, and no overlap again.

Here $L(t)$ is the overlap length of the two rectangular supports, and $A_xA$_h is the product of the pulse amplitudes. In the unit-height base case, the convolution is just the overlap length. With nonunit heights, find the same overlap length first, then scale it by $A_xA$_h.

The workflow for this lesson is to locate the edge-aligned breakpoints, write the overlap length on each nonzero region, and then multiply by the pulse amplitudes. Because the middle overlap length is constant, the final output has a trapezoidal shape: rising ramp, flat plateau, and falling ramp.

image_slots.image_description: Clean signal-plot pair on a $\tau$-axis for the worked example. Show fixed support of $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=4 with height 2$, and shifted support of $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-7 to \tau=t with height 3$. Mark the left and right edges of both supports. Include four small edge-alignment snapshots or a single annotated timeline showing first contact at $t=0$, start of full overlap at $t=4$, end of full overlap at $t=7$, and last contact at $t=11$. Avoid displaying overlap-length formulas or the final convolution output.

example_content.example_prompt: For $x(t)=2$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4 and $h(t)=3$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 7, identify the edge-aligned breakpoints of $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is that both signals are rectangular pulses with different widths. Before writing any overlap-length formula, put both supports on the $\tau$-axis: $x(\tau)$ stays fixed, and $h(t-\tau)$ slides as t changes. The heights 2 and 3 will scale the convolution later; they do not move the support edges.
Since $h(t)=3$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 7, the shifted signal $h(t-\tau)$ is nonzero when t-$\tau$ lies between 0 and 7. Solving that inequality gives the moving support of $h(t-\tau)$.
Now match the moving edges t-7 and t with the fixed edges 0 and 4 in the order those contacts occur. These four alignments are the only t-values where the overlap behavior can change.

So the ordered edge-aligned breakpoints are $t=0$, $t=4$, $t=7$, and $t=11$. These breakpoints split the convolution into no overlap, growing overlap, full overlap, shrinking overlap, and no overlap again. The next step is to use these intervals to write the overlap length; this step only identifies the control points.

image_slots.image_description: Clean $\tau$-axis overlap diagram for the worked example on the growing-overlap interval. Show fixed rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=4 with height 2$. Show the wider shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-7 to \tau=t with height 3 entering from the left during 0 \le t \le 4$. Shade only the growing overlap segment from $\tau=0 to \tau=t and label its length L(t)=t$. Mark the interval $0 \le t \le 4 as first contact through start of full overlap$. Do not show plateau, shrinking-region formulas, or the complete final convolution output.

example_content.example_prompt: For $x(t)=2$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4 and $h(t)=3$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 7, compute $y(t)$ on the growing-overlap interval 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4.

explanation_blocks.text: Use the first two breakpoints from the previous section: $t=0$ is first contact, and $t=4$ is the start of full overlap. The only task in this section is to compute the growing branch on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4.

During the growing interval, the right edge t of the shifted support has entered the fixed support, while the left edge t-7 is still to the left of 0. So the common nonzero interval starts at $\tau=0$ and ends at $\tau=t$.
The overlap length is the right endpoint minus the left endpoint. On this interval, that gives a length that grows linearly from 0 to the shorter width 4.
On the overlap, the product $x(\tau)$$h(t-\tau)$ is constant and equals 2$\cdot$ 3. Multiply the overlap length by this amplitude product to get the convolution value on the growing branch.
Thus the growing-overlap branch is $y(t)=6t$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4. This branch should not be used on the plateau or shrinking intervals; those regions have their own overlap lengths.

image_slots.image_description: Clean $\tau$-axis overlap diagram for the worked example on the full-overlap plateau. Show fixed shorter rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=4 with height 2$. Show the wider shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-7 to \tau=t with height 3 during 4 \le t \le 7$, extending beyond both edges of $x(\tau)$. Shade the entire shorter support from $\tau=0 to \tau=4 as the overlap and label its length L(t)=4$. Mark the plateau interval $4 \le t \le 7$. Do not show the growing branch, shrinking branch, or complete final convolution output.

example_content.example_prompt: For $x(t)=2$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4 and $h(t)=3$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 7, compute $y(t)$ on the full-overlap interval 4$\le$ t$\le$ 7.

explanation_blocks.text: The next interval is 4$\le$ t$\le$ 7, from the start of full overlap to the end of full overlap. The cue is containment: the shorter support is completely covered, so the overlap length stops changing.

For 4$\le$ t$\le$ 7, the left edge t-7 of the shifted support is at or to the left of $\tau=0$, and the right edge t is at or to the right of $\tau=4$. That means the whole fixed support of $x(\tau)$ is inside the shifted support of $h(t-\tau)$.
Because the overlap interval is the whole shorter support, its length is the shorter width. It does not depend on t anywhere inside the plateau interval.
Now scale that constant overlap length by the amplitude product. The product $x(\tau)$$h(t-\tau)$ equals 2$\cdot$ 3 on the entire overlap.
So the full-overlap plateau branch is $y(t)=24$ on 4$\le$ t$\le$ 7. This value is constant because the overlap length is fixed at the shorter width throughout this interval.

image_slots.image_description: Clean $\tau$-axis overlap diagram for the worked example on the shrinking-overlap interval. Show fixed rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=4 with height 2$. Show the shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-7 to \tau=t with height 3 exiting to the right during 7 \le t \le 11$. Shade only the shrinking overlap segment from $\tau=t-7 to \tau=4 and label its length L(t)=4-(t-7)=11-t$. Mark the breakpoints $t=7 and t=11 as end of full overlap and last contact$. Do not show the growing branch, plateau formula, or complete final convolution output.

example_content.example_prompt: For $x(t)=2$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4 and $h(t)=3$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 7, compute $y(t)$ on the shrinking-overlap interval 7$\le$ t$\le$ 11.

explanation_blocks.text: The shrinking interval runs from the end of full overlap at $t=7$ to last contact at $t=11$. The cue is that the shifted support is exiting to the right, so the left edge of the overlap moves while the right edge stays fixed at $\tau=4$.

For 7$\le$ t$\le$ 11, the right edge t of the shifted support is already to the right of $\tau=4$. The left edge t-7 moves from $\tau=0$ to $\tau=4$, so the remaining overlap starts at $\tau=t-7$ and ends at $\tau=4$.
The overlap length is right endpoint minus left endpoint. This gives a decreasing length, which starts at 4 when $t=7$ and reaches 0 when $t=11$.
Now multiply the shrinking overlap length by the amplitude product. The product of the two pulse heights is still 2$\cdot$ 3.
So the shrinking-overlap branch is $y(t)=6(11-t)$ on 7$\le$ t$\le$ 11. This branch decreases from the plateau value to zero, and it should only be used after the full-overlap interval ends.

image_slots.image_description: Clean instructional figure pairing the input rectangular pulses with the assembled convolution output. Show $x(t)$ with height 2 on $0 \le t \le 4 and h(t) with height 3 on 0 \le t \le 7 on compact input axes$. Below or beside them, show the trapezoidal output $y(t)$ on a t-axis with breakpoints $t=0$, $t=4$, $t=7$, and $t=11 aligned to the output regions$. Label the zero regions before 0 and after 11, the rising branch from 0 to 4, the plateau at height 24 from 4 to 7, and the shrinking branch from 7 to 11. Keep the visual clean and mathematical; do not include practice-question wording.

example_content.example_prompt: For $x(t)=2$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 4 and $h(t)=3$ on 0$\le$ t$\le$ 7, assemble the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is that all three nonzero overlap branches have already been found, so this step is not a new derivation. Assemble the output by placing each branch on the interval determined by the ordered breakpoints.
Before first contact and after last contact, the pulses do not overlap. That gives the two zero-output regions: $y(t)=0$ for $t<0$ and $y(t)=0$ for $t>11$.
Now place the branches in order. The complete convolution output is the zero branch, then the rising line, then the constant plateau, then the falling line, then the final zero branch.

As a final check, compare adjacent branch values at the shared breakpoints. The rising branch reaches the plateau at $t=4$, the shrinking branch starts at the plateau value when $t=7$, and the output returns to zero at $t=11$.
So the assembled piecewise formula is continuous at the internal breakpoints and has the expected trapezoidal shape.

Show fixed support of $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=6 with height 5$, and shifted support of $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-2 to \tau=t with height 2$. Mark the fixed edges 0 and 6 and the moving edges t-2 and t. Include simple edge-alignment snapshots or an annotated timeline showing the four contact events without displaying the final ordered breakpoint values, overlap-length formulas, or the convolution output.

prompt_blocks.text: For $x(t)=1$ on $0\let\le3$ and $h(t)=4$ on $0\let\le8$, list the ordered edge-aligned breakpoints for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0,3], and $h(t-\tau)$ has moving support [t-8,t]. Match the moving right edge t with 0 and 3 to get $t=0$ and $t=3$, then match the moving left edge t-8 with 0 and 3 to get $t=8$ and $t=11$.

prompt_blocks.text: For $x(t)=5$ on $0\let\le6$ and $h(t)=2$ on $0\let\le2$, list the ordered edge-aligned breakpoints for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0,6], and $h(t-\tau)$ has moving support [t-2,t]. Match the moving right edge t with 0 and 6 to get $t=0$ and $t=6$, then match the moving left edge t-2 with 0 and 6 to get $t=2$ and $t=8$. In order, the breakpoints are 0, 2, 6, and 8.

Show fixed rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=3 with height 2$. Show the wider shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-8 to \tau=t with height 5 entering from the left during 0 \le t \le 3$. Shade only the growing overlap segment from $\tau=0 to \tau=t$. Mark the interval $0 \le t \le 3 as first contact through start of full overlap$. Do not label the overlap-length formula, plateau region, shrinking region, or final convolution output.

Clean $\tau$-axis overlap diagram for a practice question on a shifted growing-overlap interval. Show fixed rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=1 to \tau=4 with height 4$. Show the wider shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-7 to \tau=t with height 3 entering from the left during 1 \le t \le 4$. Shade only the growing overlap segment from $\tau=1 to \tau=t$. Mark the interval $1 \le t \le 4 as first contact through start of full overlap$. Do not label the overlap-length formula, plateau region, shrinking region, or final convolution output.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=2$ on $0 \le t \le 3$ and $h(t)=5$ on $0 \le t \le 8$. Compute $y(t)$ on the growing-overlap interval $0 \le t \le 3$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the growing interval, the shifted support overlaps the fixed support from $\tau=0$ to $\tau=t$, so the overlap length is $L(t)=t$. The amplitude product is $2*5=10$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $1 \le t \le 4$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 7$. Compute $y(t)$ on the growing-overlap interval $1 \le t \le 4$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On this shifted growing interval, the common nonzero interval runs from $\tau=1$ to $\tau=t$, so the overlap length is $L(t)=t-1$. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$.

Show fixed shorter rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=3 with height 2$. Show the wider shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-8 to \tau=t with height 5 during 3 \le t \le 8$, extending beyond both edges of $x(\tau)$. Shade the entire shorter support from $\tau=0 to \tau=3 as the overlap$. Mark the plateau interval $3 \le t \le 8$. Do not label the overlap-length formula, growing branch, shrinking branch, or final convolution output.

Clean $\tau$-axis overlap diagram for a practice question on the full-overlap plateau where the shifted pulse is shorter. Show fixed longer rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=6 with height 4$. Show the shorter shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-2 to \tau=t with height 3 during 2 \le t \le 6$, fully contained inside $x(\tau)$. Shade the entire shifted shorter support from $\tau=t-2 to \tau=t as the overlap$. Mark the plateau interval $2 \le t \le 6$. Do not label the overlap-length formula, growing branch, shrinking branch, or final convolution output.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=2$ on $0 \le t \le 3$ and $h(t)=5$ on $0 \le t \le 8$. Compute $y(t)$ on the full-overlap interval $3 \le t \le 8$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the plateau, the entire shorter support is covered, so the overlap length is the shorter width, $L(t)=3$. The amplitude product is $2*5=10$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 2$. Compute $y(t)$ on the full-overlap interval $2 \le t \le 6$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Here the shifted h support is the shorter support. During full overlap, it is fully contained in $x(\tau)$, so the overlap length is $L(t)=2$. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$.

Show fixed rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=3 with height 2$. Show the shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-8 to \tau=t with height 5 exiting to the right during 8 \le t \le 11$. Shade only the shrinking overlap segment from $\tau=t-8 to \tau=3$. Mark the breakpoints $t=8 and t=11 as end of full overlap and last contact$. Do not label the overlap-length formula, growing branch, plateau formula, or final convolution output.

Clean $\tau$-axis overlap diagram for a practice question on the shrinking-overlap interval where the shifted pulse is shorter. Show fixed rectangular support $x(\tau)$ from $\tau=0 to \tau=6 with height 4$. Show the shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ from $\tau=t-2 to \tau=t with height 3 exiting to the right during 6 \le t \le 8$. Shade only the shrinking overlap segment from $\tau=t-2 to \tau=6$. Mark the breakpoints $t=6 and t=8 as end of full overlap and last contact$. Do not label the overlap-length formula, growing branch, plateau formula, or final convolution output.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=2$ on $0 \le t \le 3$ and $h(t)=5$ on $0 \le t \le 8$. Compute $y(t)$ on the shrinking-overlap interval $8 \le t \le 11$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the shrinking interval, the overlap starts at $\tau=t-8$ and ends at $\tau=3$. Its length is $3-(t-8)=11-t$, and the amplitude product is $2*5=10$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 2$. Compute $y(t)$ on the shrinking-overlap interval $6 \le t \le 8$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Here the shifted h support is exiting the fixed x support. On $6 \le t \le 8$, the overlap runs from $\tau=t-2$ to $\tau=6$, so $L(t)=6-(t-2)=8-t$. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$.

image_slots.image_description: Clean practice figure pairing the input rectangular pulses with an output-assembly guide. Show $x(t)$ with height 2 on $0 \le t \le 3 and h(t) with height 5 on 0 \le t \le 8 on compact input axes$. Below or beside them, show a blank $y(t)$ output t-axis with breakpoint markers $t=0$, $t=3$, $t=8$, and $t=11 aligned to five regions$: zero before 0, rising from 0 to 3, plateau from 3 to 8, falling from 8 to 11, and zero after 11. Do not label branch formulas, plateau height, or the completed convolution output.

Clean practice figure pairing the input rectangular pulses with an output-assembly guide. Show $x(t)$ with height 4 on $0 \le t \le 6 and h(t) with height 3 on 0 \le t \le 2 on compact input axes$, making $h(t)$ the shorter pulse. Below or beside them, show a blank $y(t)$ output t-axis with breakpoint markers $t=0$, $t=2$, $t=6$, and $t=8 aligned to five regions$: zero before 0, rising from 0 to 2, plateau from 2 to 6, falling from 6 to 8, and zero after 8. Do not label branch formulas, plateau height, or the completed convolution output.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=2$ on $0 \le t \le 3$ and $h(t)=5$ on $0 \le t \le 8$. Write the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=0$ for $t<0$; 10t for $0 \le t \le 3$; 30 for $3 \le t \le 8$; 10(11-t) for $8 \le t \le 11$; 0 for $t>11$

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The ordered breakpoints are 0, 3, 8, and 11. The amplitude product is $2*5=10$, so the growing and shrinking branches scale the overlap length by 10, and the plateau value is $10*3=30$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 2$. Write the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=0$ for $t<0$; 12t for $0 \le t \le 2$; 24 for $2 \le t \le 6$; 12(8-t) for $6 \le t \le 8$; 0 for $t>8$

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The ordered breakpoints are 0, 2, 6, and 8 because h is the shorter pulse. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$, so the plateau value is $12*2=24$ and the falling branch uses the final-contact time 8.
